title: Affine etale atlas of a quasi-compact algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Give $|X|$, the field-valued point classes, the quotient topology of a surjective etale scheme atlas [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Assume that $|X|$ is quasi-compact, meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover. Then there exist an affine $S$-scheme $W$ and a representable surjective etale morphism $h_W\to X$. Here affine means isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$, and etale and representable have the meanings of [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. No separatedness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose the atlas $p:h_U\to X$ supplied by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], with $U=\coprod_{d\in D}U_d$ and each $U_d$ affine over $S$. Its point map is surjective and its quotient topology is the topology stipulated for $|X|$. Thus this is an atlas to which [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] applies.

Apply [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] to $p$ and the assumed quasi-compact space $|X|$. It gives a finite subset $D_0\subseteq D$ such that $W=\coprod_{d\in D_0}U_d$, an open subscheme of $U$, has a representable surjective etale restriction $p|_W:h_W\to X$. Its $S$-structure is the restriction of that of $U$. No property of intersections of affine opens is used.

source.place: Tags 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), finite-subcover step, and 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), restriction to a finite component subatlas.

proof.text: For each $d\in D_0$ write $U_d\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{d\in D_0}A_d)$, so $W$ is affine in precisely the absolute sense required in the statement. Together with the restriction from step 2 this proves the conclusion. If $|X|=\varnothing$, the finite-subatlas lemma permits $D_0=\varnothing$; the empty product is the zero ring and the same coproduct-spectrum isomorphism gives $W=\operatorname{Spec}0$.

Statement and stmt_deps match clones/live and side-live exactly. Source: Stacks spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), forward direction, together with 03FX and 03E4. The 'finite surjective' at the end of the source proof is a typo for étale surjective; the report's counterexample A^1 ⊔ G_m → A^1 is correct, and the item never claims finiteness. Step 1: lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover gives a disjoint-affine representable surjective étale atlas and an atlas-independent quotient topology in which every |t| is continuous. Hence that topology equals the final topology of def-a1-space-point-topology used by the next lemma (the definition node also says so), and |X| quasi-compactness carries over. Step 2: the first clause of lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas has exactly these hypotheses and gives a finite D0 with the restriction representable surjective étale, including D0 = ∅. No intersections of affines are used, so no separatedness is needed. Step 3: the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum (sigmaSpec, finite IsIso) gives W ≅ Spec of the product of the A_d. The step is correctly elementary, since finitely many disjoint open summands form the coproduct, and the empty case gives Spec 0. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. Small cases checked: empty X, affine X, an infinite atlas over compact |X|, and a non-quasi-separated X. The two off-unit sk-p-real-rankin nodes are generic algebraic-space tools and are declared in tool_uses; accepted.
